title: Derby Day parties at home and visitors sent to her parents
summary: Every Derby Day the family held an all-day party with food, cards and checkers and watched the horses from the back field. Later she sent friends she met while travelling to visit her parents in Kentucky.

Mama would fix up a whole lot of stuff and we'd just be eating and drinking. A little egg nog, you know, and little mint julips. Of course they was kind of weak, you know. Just as long as we felt we had one we was happy.
Would you have the radio going so you'd hear what was going on?

They used to have those loud speakers and you could sit on the front porch and hear the horses run. But you know, we would have the party. We would just be there eating and drinking and just having fun and cards and checkers and what have you, all day until time to go and then they'd let us in the back field for nothing. And we'd go along and we'd see the horses run.
Yeah, and they charge you a whole lot to get in there now.

I'll bet they do. And people coming from all over to get in there.
Yeah. You can't get in there now without paying, but we used to go up there and go right on in.
Did every body take off on Derby Day? Would your father, would he be there? Or would people work use the same?

He worked just the hours he wanted to anyway, most of the time. He'd go out on Derby Day. Alot of times he would just come on home, you know, and just help make everybody comfortable. And I know when I got around and traveled I used to tell all my friends I'd meet, I said, 'well if you ever go to Kentucky, go go and see my Mother and Fater'. And they would and they would make me feel so nice.
And you mother and father were pleases.
Oh yes. They would write a letter that such and such a person came by to see us and they cooked dinner and everything.
